chunks: And by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, then they will not find in their hearts any discomfort from what you have judged and they will submit with [full] submission.

key_terms.يُحَكِّمُوكَ: make you judge / appoint you as arbitrator

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for true belief regarding the Prophet's judicial rulings according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as the foundational proof for the infallibility and binding authority of the Prophet's (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) judgments, extending to the Imams who inherit his judicial role. The phrase 'until they make you judge' (yuhakkimuka) highlights the necessity of active referral to the Imam in disputes, while 'no reluctance in their hearts' (la yajidū fī anfusihim harajan) underscores the spiritual perfection required to accept rulings even when they contradict personal desires. This dual condition of external submission and internal contentment distinguishes true faith from mere nominal adherence.
